title: Is it haram to date?
hookLine: the most-asked question: what's agreed, what's discussed, and why a feeling isn't a sin

lines: AGREED, DISCUSSED, AND NOT A SIN.
cards: It's the question a lot of young Muslims ask a search bar before they'd ever ask a parent: is it haram to date? Sometimes it comes with a name attached. Someone from chemistry class.
Someone from the group chat. Sometimes it isn't really about rules at all, but about a feeling, and whether having it makes you a bad person. The answers online tend to shout.
Here's the calmer version: what's agreed, what's discussed, and what isn't a sin at all.

teach.b: Start with what nearly every Muslim scholar agrees on. Sex belongs inside marriage, nikah. The Qur'an puts it as a fence, not just a rule: “And come not near unto adultery. Lo! it is an abomination and an evil way.”

Come not near. That's why many teachers also advise against being secluded alone together; a hadith in Tirmidhi says that when a man and a woman are alone, the third with them is Shaytan. Now what's discussed.
Dating, the way movies use the word, usually means a private relationship, with no plan, and physical closeness. Most scholars say that's outside the lines.
But getting to know someone for marriage is different, and the hadith encourage it. A companion told the Prophet ﷺ he'd proposed to a woman. Have you seen her? the Prophet asked.

teach.h: GO AND LOOK AT HER: ENCOURAGED.
teach.b: Go and look at her, he said, for that is more likely to make things last between you. That's in Tirmidhi.
So how do people meet and talk? Here, communities draw the line in different places. Some families arrange introductions.
Some allow conversations with a parent or chaperone nearby, or in public places. Some people use apps built for marriage. Many call it getting to know someone with intention.
Your own family and teachers will have a view, and they won't all match.
And the part people most need to hear: a feeling isn't a sin. Camp two met the hadith that Allah forgives what the soul whispers, as long as it isn't acted on. Liking someone is human.
And Ibn Majah reports the Prophet saying: nothing has been seen like marriage, for two people who love each other.

how: Many Muslim families and communities encourage getting to know a possible spouse with marriage in mind, through introductions, family involvement, public meetings or marriage-focused apps, and keep physical closeness for marriage; where the lines fall varies by family and teacher.

o: marriage, the contract that joins two people
a dowry gift paid to the bride's family
an engagement party before the wedding

games.q: what's inside today — tap the pairs.
p: not a sin; acting on it is a choice

s: in Islam, having a crush is itself a sin
a hadith says Allah forgives what the soul whispers, as long as it isn't acted on.
the Prophet ﷺ told a man to see the woman he'd proposed to
Tirmidhi: go and look at her, for that is more likely to make things last between you.
all Muslim families draw the same line on how couples meet
some arrange introductions, some allow chaperoned or public meetings; views differ.

games.q: a companion tells the Prophet ﷺ he has proposed to a woman he has never seen. what does the Prophet say?
games.why: go and look at her, for that is more likely to make things last between you (Tirmidhi).

practice: Think of a strong pull you're carrying: a crush, a craving, the urge to send a message at midnight. Don't push it away, and don't follow it; let it sit beside you, the way you'd sit beside a friend who's upset.
On each breath out, feel the space between the feeling and the act, and notice you're still the one choosing.

wordCard.voice: Nikah. Marriage, the contract that makes a home of two people; the place the tradition gives to closeness, and the reason for getting to know someone.

orig.note: Arabic: marriage, the marriage contract; the Qur'an uses the same root for marrying.

carryVoice: Your line: a feeling isn't a sin. What you do with it is the choice. That's day one hundred forty-four.

sources.q: And come not near unto adultery. Lo! it is an abomination and an evil way.
